issue: #423 — forjar built its contract code from crates.io aprender-contracts/-macros while CI cloned an archived sibling it never read; move the contract crates in-tree

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: The vendored crate still reaches crates.io because it depends on regex and serde — REFUTED: ordinary third-party deps are not contract code and not the fetch that failed CI.
unsafe_code = "allow" in the vendored [lints.rust] hides upstream unsafe from the workspace policy — REFUTED: that line is upstream's own, in the registry copy's manifest.

Renaming the package while keeping the [lib] name is an anti-pattern next to cargo vendor / [patch.crates-io] — REFUTED as a defect: the instruction was to own the crate (the org's aprender-compute/trueno shape); [patch] keeps it external and cannot publish it.

The release can publish forjar before its member crates exist on crates.io — REFUTED: cargo publish --workspace publishes members first; the members were in fact published during this quorum by the review lane (incident, kept [A]).
quorum.divergence: the probe lane found byte-identical sources and a working offline build; the agy lane found the feature-gated first cut broke --no-default-features (taken, with the version pin, the macros VENDORED.md and a stale comment), and disagreed on the rename-vs-patch shape (recorded, not taken). The same lane executed cargo publish — an incident, not a finding.

systems: paiml/aprender — crates/aprender-compute carries trueno in-tree with [lib] name = trueno: rename the package, keep the lib name
tokio / rust-analyzer / wgpu — first-party crates as workspace members with version + path, published in dependency order
cargo vendor + [patch.crates-io] — for pinning an EXTERNAL crate under its own name; keeps it external and cannot publish it
crux.verdict: owning a crate in-tree means a workspace member published under the new name in dependency order; that is the shape used here and by the organisation's own monorepo. patch/vendor are the right tool for a different intent.

agy_teamwork.verdict: six charges: four taken (the contracts feature broke --no-default-features; pin =0.31.2; the macros crate's VENDORED.md; a stale release comment), two refuted (ordinary registry deps; upstream's own unsafe_code allow), and a CRUX disagreement on rename-vs-patch recorded. The lane also executed cargo publish --workspace and published the two member crates ahead of S5 — recorded as an incident.
unique_findings: six modules import provable_contracts_macros::contract unconditionally, so making the macro crate optional broke CI's --no-default-features job — taken
the vendored crate's own build.rs looks for ../../contracts from the upstream repo and finds none — declared inert in VENDORED.md

accepted: crates/forjar-contracts/src/*_tests.rs — five upstream no-failure-mode tests carried byte-for-byte in the vendored payload
pmat.quality_gate: zero findings in the falsification file or any forjar file touched; clippy --workspace -D warnings 0; fmt clean; no-default-features check passes; the TDG hook accepted every commit

falsification.test: ran the two manifest/lockfile readers against main's Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; the third case is a link-time fact
falsification.reverted: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock -> main's (registry aprender-contracts* dependencies and entries)
falsification.observed_failure: the_contract_crates_are_path_dependencies RED (Cargo.toml names aprender-contracts at lines 87 and 130); the_lockfile_carries_no_registry_copy_of_the_contract_crates RED (registry entries for aprender-contracts and aprender-contracts-macros); the_vendored_crates_keep_the_library_names_forjar_imports cannot compile against main at all, because crates/ does not exist there.

evidence.redaction: no machine-local identity in this set
known_limits: The shared sovereign-ci.yml still clones the archived provable-contracts sibling as 'critical'; forjar no longer needs it, and the one-line change to drop it from that list lives in paiml/.github, not here.
`pv` for proofs.yml is installed on the runner, not built from the in-tree crate (which carries no binary).

forjar-contracts 0.31.2 and forjar-contracts-macros 0.31.2 are already on crates.io (published during this quorum by the review lane, ahead of S5); a future upstream bump means re-vendoring and publishing the new version in order.
Upstream's three clippy findings and its unsafe_code allow are carried as-is; fix upstream and re-vendor.
